items.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: And then Lenny White became the producer, which worked out for me, and we took all those fusion tunes and turned them into R&B.

ctx.x: That’s good. All that preparation paid off.

Musically never. I’ve left things that I didn’t like, but musically never, I’ve never had one go bad on me or one that I couldn’t do, whether it was R&B, funk, whatever it was, I could still do it. But preference now is bop, or getting a little out here and there, but the preference is bop. But no I’ve never had anything go bad. When I did the album on Motown in ’83, it was Bobby M. Blow, it was a funk R&B record. And when I first got the contract when Rick got me that contract, I had all these grandiose ideas of…

make it R&B and I’m going to blow funky, less notes, do the whole bit. And it did very well actually. But my brother could never understand this in my nature, but I didn’t want to do a second, they didn’t pick up a second anyways, but I wouldn’t have done a second. And I decided, and my brother says, “You could be rich, I mean you could do this well.” I says, “I know I could do it well but now that I’ve done it I have to do it because that’s what the people hear, the record. So now I have to play that. But I…
